title: A Data-dependent Early Stopping Rule using Rademacher Complexity with L1-norm
abstract: arXiv:2608.24210v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training neural networks requires balancing the trade-off between fitting the training data and achieving robust performance on unseen inputs. This ability, commonly referred to as generalizability, is determined by the gap between the empirical risk on the training set (``empirical loss'') and the expected risk over the data distribution (``generalization error''). Existing approaches typically estimate the generalization error numerically, requiring gradient descent training and an ``early stopping'' strategy. In this work, we introduce an analytic framework that estimates the optimal time of early stopping without the need for training. Several works in the literature also give such analytical estimations, but they are generally based on random matrix theory and often make assumptions on the distribution of the data or the eigenvalue distribution of the covariance matrix. translated_title: 一种基于Rademacher复杂度与L1范数的数据依赖早停规则
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24210v1 公告类型：新 摘要：训练神经网络需要在拟合训练数据与在未见输入上实现稳健性能之间取得平衡。这种能力通常称为泛化性，由训练集上的经验风险（“经验损失”）与数据分布上的期望风险（“泛化误差”）之间的差距决定。现有方法通常数值估计泛化误差，需要梯度下降训练和“早停”策略。在本工作中，我们引入了一个分析框架，无需训练即可估计早停的最佳时间。文献中也有几项工作提供此类分析估计，但它们通常基于随机矩阵理论，并对数据分布或协方差矩阵的特征值分布作出假设。相比之下，我们的工作基于Rademacher复杂度（RC）与L1范数。
tldr: 本文提出一种无需训练、基于Rademacher复杂度和L1范数的分析框架，用于数据依赖地估计神经网络早停的最优时间，避免了对数据分布或协方差矩阵的常见假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an analytic framework based on Rademacher complexity with L1-norm to estimate the optimal early stopping time for neural networks without training, avoiding common assumptions on data or covariance eigenvalue distributions.
